properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 9:57AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

San Juan River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Farmington.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, The current extent of flooding along the
San Juan River in New Mexico has not been observed since before the
completion of Navajo Dam in 1962. In the Farmington vicinity,
backwater flooding on the Animas River at and above the confluence
with the San Juan River is the major concern. See flood bulletins
pertaining to the Animas River. Downriver through Shiprock, mostly
low lying and agricultural areas are subject to inundation. At 8.5
feet, Overbank flow is occurring from just below the confluence of
the Animas and San Juan Rivers at Farmington, and continuing
downriver through Shiprock. At this water level, the fast flow can
result in river bank erosion but otherwise minor flood damage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 AM MDT Friday the stage was 11.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:00 AM MDT Friday was 11.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 12.2 feet
late this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late
tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.3
feet on 09/06/1909.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 11:23AM EDT until October 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves
expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Ocean overwash impacts will improve some this morning
as seas continue to subside. However, seas build some tonight
through the weekend which may bring additional minor overwash in
areas were dunes have been compromised. NC-12 between the
Basnight Bridge and Rodanthe remains closed. Today's high tide
is around 6 pm this evening. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around noon today.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 23 at 9:39AM AST until October 24 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to
12 feet. For the HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, life-threatening rip
current.

* WHERE... For the HIGH SURF ADVISORY, the most vulnerable areas
for high surf and beach erosion include Pinones along Road 187,
Parcelas Suarez, Villas del Mar, and Villa Christiana in Loiza;
Fortuna in Luquillo; Pueblo and Tamarindo in Aguadilla; Bario
Obrero, Pueblo and Jareaito in Arecibo; Las Boca in Barceloneta;
Machuca in Manati; Puerto Nuevo in Vega Baja; Ocean Park in San
Juan; and Barrio Espinal in Aguada. For the HIGH RIP CURRENT
RISK, beaches along the west to northeast coast of Puerto Rico.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory remains until 6 PM AST this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk remains through Saturday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...FOR THE HIGH SURF ADVISORY, High waves that can wash
over jetties and sweep people and pets onto jagged rocks.
Rough surf may also knock you down. Large breaking waves will
result in localized beach/dune structure erosion and dangerous
swimming conditions. FOR THE HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.areaDesc: Rio Grande, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 6:50AM MDT until October 25 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

.Heavy rainfall across the eastern San Juan mountains and the upper
Rio Grande will cause high flows with moderate flooding expected at
Del Norte late this morning. The flood crest is expected to reach
6.60 feet, which is just below a previous record flood crest of 6.80
feet.

For the Upper Rio Grande River...including Del Norte...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande  near Del Norte.

* WHEN...Until Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.5 feet, Moderate Flood. Water flows over low spots
in Hanna Lane Road west of Del Norte. Water threatens homes and RV
park near Del Norte Park in Del Norte. Homes near First Street and
the Oak Street Bridge on Colorado Highway 112 are threatened by
high water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:31 AM MDT Friday the stage was 6.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:31 AM MDT Friday was 6.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.6 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.4
feet on 06/29/1927.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 700 PM MDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 8:43AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend. There
is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage next week,
after northeast winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EDT Friday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EDT Friday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet today, with additional rises within Moderate
Flood Stage this weekend.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 5:17AM MST until October 24 at 3:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Holbrook to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until 300 AM MST /400 AM MDT/ Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring. Further rises in the water levels are expected. Deadly
flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 515 AM MST /615 AM MDT/, a river gauge reported falling water
levels at Woodruff, however elevated flow reminded from Holbrook
to Winslow. Elevated flow is forecast to continue through this
afternoon, with downstream impacts at Birdsprings likely later
this evening.
- For the Little Colorado River at Holbrook:
At 4:30am MST /5:30am MDT/ the stage was 14.34 feet.
Flood Stage is 15.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 16.41 feet is expected at 1:00pm MST /2:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 15.5 feet: Railroad bridge affected. Overflow on South Bank.

For the Little Colorado River at Joseph City:
At 4:30am MST /5:30am MDT/ the stage was 5.57 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 6.5 feet is expected at 2:00pm MST /3:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: Potential downstream lowland overflow.
At 9.0 feet: Flood stage. Minor overflow on right (north) bank,
with no threat to any buildings, mainly rural countryside.

For Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 5:00am MST /6:00am MDT/ the stage was 17.26 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels remain above action stage through 10:00am
MST /11:00am MDT/ Saturday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.


- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 23 at 4:59AM MDT until October 24 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central and west central New Mexico,
including the following areas, in north central New Mexico, Far
Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains and Northwest Highlands. In
west central New Mexico, West Central Highlands and West Central
Mountains.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Scattered-to-numerous showers and thunderstorms will continue
today and this evening. Some of today's stronger storms will be
capable of producing rain at rates up to 1 inch per hour. Some
locations will receive repeated rounds of storms with over 1.5
inches of additional rain accumulation possible. Locations where
the ground is saturated from heavy rain that fell on Thursday
will be favored for rapid runoff and flash flooding, even from
only moderate rainfall today.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM NOON TODAY TO 8 PM MDT
THIS EVENING DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR SLOPE AND
BOWMAN COUNTIES...

.Very warm and breezy conditions are expected across southwest North
Dakota this afternoon into early this evening. In far southwest North
Dakota, afternoon relative humidities are expected to drop to 15 to
20 percent, with winds around 20 mph and gusts to 40 mph. Therefore a
Red Flag Warning has been issued for Bowman and Slope counties in far
southwest North Dakota.

burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:

either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity and warm temperatures can contribute to extreme
fire behavior.

expected near Togiak.

* WHERE...Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...10 AM Friday to 7AM Saturday

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Bering front arrives to the Southwest

result in elevated water levels and high surf. This period of
winds will coincide with two tidal cycles and push water
levels 1.0 to 2.0 feet above the normal highest tide line.

as winds decrease, alleviating coastal concerns.

properties.description:

above the normal highest tide line, and 35 to 50 mph winds
with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...8 AM Friday through 1 AM Saturday, particularly around
high tides near 10 AM and 10 PM Friday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely scenario is for water
levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide line.
While unlikely, the worst case scenario for Kipnuk is for
water levels to be 3.5 to 4.0 feet above the normal high tide
line, while the worst case for Kwigillingok is 4.0 to 5.0 feet
above the normal high tide line. The 10 PM Friday peak, with
the aforementioned high tide, is expected to be the higher of
the two peaks. We are closely monitoring this storm. In the
meantime, please have a plan in place.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

* IMPACTS: Low humidities, unseasonably warm temperatures, strong
gusty winds, and a wind shift with a cold front will create
erratic fire behavior and difficult control of new or existing
fires.

In North Central WY Fire Zone...274.
In Southeast MT Fire Zone...131.
In Southeast MT and Northwest SD Fire Zone...133.

In North Central WY...Sheridan.
In Northwest SD...Harding.
In South Central MT...Big Horn.
In Southeast MT...Carter...Fallon...Powder River...Rosebud
Treasure.

a Baker Montana to Sheridan Wyoming line.

* WIND: Southwest 20 to 30 mph gusting up to 45 mph. Winds shifting
to the northwest behind a late day cold front, with continued

crossings.

the Little Colorado River from the confluence with the Moenkopi

stage.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.

and fall below flood stage late Friday morning.

lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Moenkopi and Salt Trail Canyon. - This includes the following
recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Blue Water Base Camp and Old Fish Camp Site.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:

unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant
coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Mainland
Northern Brevard, Northern Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland
Southern Brevard and Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Saturday
night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 2 AM Saturday to 2
AM EDT Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Saturday
night through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Some roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Shoreline erosion may occur. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
properties.instruction:
Conditions favorable for coastal flooding are expected to
develop. Coastal residents should be alert for later statements
or warnings and take necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Northwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Wilbur, Disautel Pass, Odessa, Badger Mountain Road,
Mansfield, Waterville, Harrington, Grand Coulee, Bridgeport,
Okanogan, Omak, Ritzville, Oroville, Brewster, Nespelem, Coulee
City, Tonasket, and Creston.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
Motorists traveling along Highway 2 between Creston and Douglas
should take extra precaution and be prepared for strong cross
winds. Patchy blowing dust will be possible. New fire starts could
spread swiftly through dry fuel beds, especially in the afternoon
as humidity values lower near 20 percent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will increase after midnight with peak
gusts between 3AM and 11AM. The axis of strongest winds will be
through the Okanogan Valley, across northwestern Douglas County and
into northern Grant and western Lincoln County between Creston and
Coulee City.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 12:01AM MDT until October 23 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until noon MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.
Low-water crossings are inundated with water and may not be
passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1201 AM MDT, Doppler radar and gauges indicated heavy rain.
Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned
area.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
East Mancos River, West Mancos River,  Middle Mancos River, Ute
Canyon, West Fork Mud Creek, Lewis Creek, Lost Canyon Creek, East
Canyon, and Mancos River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mancos and Mesa Verde Natl Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL NOON MDT TODAY

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:51PM MDT until October 24 at 12:19AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs, Bluff...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 14.5 feet, Water has reached the foundations of some
homes in the San Juan River Ranch northeast of Pagosa Springs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 PM MDT Thursday the stage was 13.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 PM MDT Thursday was 13.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 15.0 feet late tonight. It will
then fall below flood stage tomorrow evening to 8.0 feet Saturday
evening. It will rise to 8.1 feet Sunday morning. It will then
fall again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 13.5
feet on 06/29/1927.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued late Friday night at 1230 AM MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 23 at 12:32PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 97W continues to develop over the northern Marshall Islands,
centered near 11N166E in the vicinity of Bikini and Rongelap Atolls.
97W is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA)
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), meaning it is expected
to develop into a significant tropical cyclone (a tropical
depression) within 24 hours. Himawari visible satellite imagery this
afternoon shows numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms across
the northern Marshall Islands, focused mainly over the
northwesternmost islands and atolls. Scatterometry data from this
morning shows fresh to strong west winds near Ujae and Ebadon Atolls,
and surface observations on Kwajalein Island are showing fresh west
winds with frequent strong gusts. Near-gale force gusts have been
observed with passing showers, and significant boat damage was
recently reported along west-facing exposures of Kwajalein as well.

Surging west winds are expected to continue across the western and
central Marshall Islands, south of Invest 97W's center, and boats
should be safely moved from west-facing exposures and secured, if
possible. Fresh to strong west winds will begin to shift
southwesterly tonight as 97W strengthens, and persist through Sunday
as 97W begins to lift north out of the RMI. Locally heavy showers
will be possible across the northern half of the Marshall Islands
through the weekend. Showers and winds will begin to diminish Sunday
night as 97W pulls farther away, but elevated west to southwest swell
associated with the disturbance may persist into early next week.
Elevated surf along west and south reefs may become hazardous this
weekend into early next week as these swells persist. This situation
will be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall
Islands.

For more information on Invest 97W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

NWSheadline: INVEST 97W DEVELOPING OVER THE NORTHERN MARSHALL ISLANDS, NOW THE SUBJECT OF A TROPICAL CYCLONE FORMATION ALERT... ...LOCALLY HEAVY SHOWERS, SURGING WEST WINDS AND SWELL EXPECTED

properties.description:
AQAHGX

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Friday, October 23, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Friday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:
Ozone: The Facts www.tceq.texas.gov/airquality/monops/ozonefacts.html
EPA AirNow: www.airnow.gov/?city=Houston&state=TX&country=USA

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 22 at 3:08PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
The following statement was issued by the Oklahoma Department of
Environmental Quality until 10 PM CDT Saturday evening.

An Air Quality Alert for Ozone has been issued for Friday, October
23rd for the Oklahoma City Metropolitan area due to expected high
concentrations of ozone.

Public Health Recommendations: Persons with existing heart or
respiratory ailments should reduce physical exertion and outdoor
activity.

The general public is encouraged to help alleviate the problem by
reducing vehicle miles traveled by riding the bus, carpooling, or
avoiding unnecessary trips. The public is also asked to avoid
refueling during the morning and early afternoon hours, and to avoid
the use of two cycle engines such as lawn mowers, motorcycles, weed
trimmers, and outboard engines. It is also advised to limit outdoor
burning.

To view the latest air quality map, visit airnow.gov or the AirNow
app.

For hourly updates on concentrations and possible health warnings,
telephone the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality at
405-702-4100. For more information on health effects, call the
American Lung Association of Oklahoma at 405-748-4674
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 12:07PM MDT until October 23 at 12:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is occurring.
Prolonged and widespread moderate to heavy rainfall will continue
trough this evening. This coupled with near-saturated soils will
allow flows to remain high across all waterways within the warned
area, including all of the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area.
High flows are expected to continue within, but not limited to...
the Paria River, Wahweep Creek, Warm Creek, Last Chance Creek,
Croton Canyon, and the Escalante River Basin and tributaries. Many
backcountry roads within this area are expected to become
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1154 AM MDT, Widespread flooding is already occurring in the
warned area. A recent example is the Escalante River near
Escalante reaching a new high flow for this event of 1660 cfs
over the last hour. After reaching a peak of 2500 cfs on the
Paria River last evening, flows have decreased but continue to
run high and swift, and additional rises remain likely. Between 1
and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 1215 PM MDT FRIDAY

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Emery County in central Utah...
Southeastern Sevier County in central Utah...
Northwestern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Eastern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Northeastern Kane County in southern Utah...
Wayne County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1115 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Prolonged and
widespread moderate to heavy rainfall will continue into tonight
before dissipating. This coupled with near-saturated soils will
allow rapidly increasing flows across all waterways within the
warned area, including all of Capitol Reef National Park, and the
San Rafael Swell south of I-70. Increasingly high flows are

the Dirty Devil and its tributaries, and slot canyons within the
San Rafael Reef.

occurring along the Fremont River which has closed Highway 24
between mile markers 80-86. Between 0.5 and 1.6 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hanksville, Capitol Reef National Park, Torrey, Hite Marina,
Ticaboo, Teasdale, Bullfrog, Halls Crossing, Caineville, Goblin
Valley and Fruita.
